subject: Post-demo: pricing & context profile for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: pricing & context profile for Acme Retail

Hi Tom — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so the team can move toward a trial: 

Recap (short):
- Primary use: customer support summarization + contextual retrieval for reps.
- Typical session: a short user prompt followed by a multi-paragraph generated reply.
- Key unknowns we flagged: monthly active sessions, average prompt/completion token mix, and percent of sessions that need long-context (32k/128k).

Information we captured during call (please confirm):
- Target rollout: Q3 pilot across Support (approx 500–1,000 reps initially).
- Expected monthly sessions (ballpark): you mentioned ~500k active sessions/month — please confirm final number and whether sessions are multi-turn.
- Desired unit cost target: you said leadership aims for ~"$3k per 1M tokens" as a procurement target — can you confirm whether that’s a hard constraint or a negotiable goal?

Initial context profiling for pricing (please confirm/change):
- Average prompt tokens per session (estimate): 400 tokens
- Average completion tokens per session (estimate): 1,800 tokens
- Long-context need: ~10% of sessions require >32k context (search + doc window), ~2% may need 128k for full-thread retrieval

Next steps / asks from Acme: 
1) Confirm monthly session volume (and % multi-turn).
2) Confirm whether 10% / 2% long-context split looks right or if you expect more long-form generation.
3) Loop in procurement contact (PO process) so we can issue a formal quote for the pilot.

What I’ll deliver: updated cost worksheet with 3 scenarios (Hosted pay-as-you-go, 12-month committed discount, and Dedicated reserved capacity) attached — includes token math and projected $/1M tokens to hit your $3k target.

Attached: Redwood-Acme-pricing-draft.xlsx (sheet: ContextSizing) — I’ll update after your confirmation on volumes.

If this aligns, I’ll schedule a short follow-up with our Solutions Engineer (Dylan) to map the Dedicated sizing vs hosted trade-offs.

Thanks,
— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming sessions: target for pilot is ~600k sessions/month (these are largely single-turn, but support agents may do 1–2 follow-ups in ~15% of cases).
- Token averages (measured off a small prototype): average prompt ~420 tokens, average completion ~1,750 tokens. We have a long-tail for some escalation cases where agents paste entire ticket histories (that’s where the 32k/128k question comes in).
- Long-context frequency: roughly 12% need 32k-range context, 3% of sessions are very long (128k) — these are infrequent but business-critical.
- Budget: Leadership gave a guideline of $75k–$95k for the pilot; $3k/1M tokens is our target but we can consider committed spend to get a better rate.

Looping Kate (procurement) — Kate, happy to connect on PO/timing.

Tom Reynolds

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & context profile for Acme Retail

Tom — perfect, thanks for the numbers. I ran the initial token math with your confirmed averages and the pilot budget band. See the quick calc below (high-level):

Calculation (monthly):
- Sessions: 600,000
- Avg prompt tokens: 420 => prompt total = 252M tokens
- Avg completion tokens: 1,750 => completion total = 1,050M tokens
- Overhead (system + metadata + tokenization variance): ~5% => +~65M tokens
- Estimated total tokens/month = ~1,367M tokens (~1.37B)

At $3,000 per 1M tokens => estimated monthly cost = $4.1M (obviously outside budget).
At $3,000 per 1M is not feasible without significant discounts / committed discounts. However, with committed reserved capacity or Dedicated blocks we can materially reduce unit price. Example scenarios (very rough):
- Hosted PAYG (no commit): unit $/1M tokens ~= $3,200–$4,500 (depends on model family + context length utilization)
- 12-month committed tier (moderate commit): unit $/1M tokens ~= $1,800–$2,800
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + quantization/throughput tuning): unit $/1M tokens ~= $1,200–$2,000 (with high utilization and caching)

Observations and levers to hit your target:
1) Reduce average completion length via prompt engineering / structured responses (saves ~30–40% of token load if feasible).
2) Use prefix caching and KV cache aggressively for repeated context (search/KB hits).
3) Commit to a 6–12 month reserved volume to access enterprise discounts (we can model a 40–60% reduction off pay-as-you-go).
4) Offload the infrequent 128k sessions to a specialized path (larger context model billed separately only when used).

Action items from Redwood:
- I’ll update the attached cost sheet with three concrete price scenarios (Hosted PAYG, Committed 12mo, Dedicated pilot) and include a target break-even at $3k/1M tokens to show required commit.
- Dylan to propose a Dedicated pilot sizing based on actual throughput needs and latency SLOs.

Can you confirm whether you’d prefer Redwood to: 
A) Propose a 3-month pilot on Hosted with a committed $X spend to reach $3k target, or
B) Size a Dedicated pilot (1 month ramp + 11 months reserved) and present an enterprise quote?

Attached: acme-context-breakdown.csv (includes the token math shown above).

— Soojin

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & context profile for Acme Retail

Quick engineering note for sizing (internal):
- If 12% of sessions need ~32k and 3% need 128k, the effective token-per-request for model selection increases significantly because of KV / attention window behavior. For budget estimates assume ~1.25x multiplier on completion tokens to account for longer context for those sessions (we used 1.25 in the attached sheet).
- Caching: With good prefix/KV caching we can reduce repeated retrieval token cost on ~40% of sessions; worth instrumenting early in the trial.
- Dedicated pilot: propose a 4-GPU node pool (A100 or equivalent) with autoscale up to 8 nodes for peak; enable quantization for cold-start cost savings and set a fallback to smaller model for sub-200-token completions.
- Latency: heavy long-context sessions (128k) will have higher tail latency. Plan SLOs around p95 for critical routes and use async batch workers for non-interactive exports.

I’ll draft a short Sizing + Ops note for the pilot and drop into our Drive for Soojin to send to Acme.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
